editorialPromise: One useful idea about visual communication, demonstrated with an editable example.
audience: People making their first repeatable brand media system.

identity.intent: Curious, clear and playful, with enough space for the idea to be understood.
identity.guidance: These are authored hypotheses. Musical settings are reproducible choices; recognition, warmth and fit require listening.
identity.signature: No signature has been approved. The generator's spoken Lolly tag is explicitly off in these candidates.

modes.label: Explain
modes.purpose: Help a listener follow a new idea, especially beneath narration.
modes.direction: Leave room around the voice. Restraint is a choice about this use, not a universal definition of clarity.
modes.visual: One hierarchy, generous space, restrained fades. Keep the source values visible.
listenFor: Can every word be followed at a comfortable level?
Does the bed help without making the explanation feel sleepy?
Is the ending deliberate or merely faded?
modes.counterexample: A prominent lead or voice effect competes with the narrator. Removing all motion can also hide the point being explained.

modes.label: Demonstrate
modes.purpose: Show how a choice changes the work while keeping the process legible.
modes.direction: A steady pulse can support a sequence of actions. Do not pretend an action is synchronised to a beat unless its timing was authored.
modes.visual: Show a before and an after with identical source facts. Reveal each step at a phrase boundary.
listenFor: Do visual steps and spoken phrases agree?
Is the pulse useful rather than hurried?
Does this feel related to Explain despite the different arrangement?
modes.counterexample: Fast cuts conceal the changed variable. Decorative effects imply that unchanged data has changed.

modes.label: Play
modes.purpose: Invite exploration when the music or expressive motion has room to lead.
modes.direction: Allow a more audible melody and brighter rhythm. Use a quieter mix whenever narration needs attention.
modes.visual: More expressive entrances and colour use, with the same type, factual core and readable ending.
listenFor: Is the melody enjoyable over repeated listening?
Does the family resemblance survive the brighter treatment?
Does speech stay understandable after the bed returns?
modes.counterexample: Continuous novelty makes every edition sound unrelated. A new seed alone does not establish an editorial reason to publish.

stories.title: Same numbers. Different impression.
stories.script: These two values are forty and fifty. Starting a bar chart at zero shows their full relationship. Cropping the axis can make the difference look much larger. Keep the numbers visible, explain the scale, and choose a presentation that helps the reader judge the difference.
stories.source: Original synthetic values for this demonstration. No external measurement or live feed.

stories.title: Let motion point to the change.
stories.script: A moving shape attracts attention. In this example, only the value that changes needs emphasis. Keep the labels still, give the movement time to settle, and leave a readable final frame. The motion should help explain the change, while the numbers remain the source of truth.
stories.keyPoint: Emphasise the changed value; keep the labels readable.
stories.source: Original explanatory example using the same synthetic values, forty and fifty.

stories.title: One identity can speak in different tones.
stories.script: The picture and the words stay the same. Listen to how a restrained bed, a steady pulse, and a brighter melody change the feeling. A sonic identity can allow all three. Choose the sound for the situation, keep recognisable anchors, and check that the voice still comes through.
stories.keyPoint: Keep the anchors. Choose the expression for the situation.
stories.source: Original listening prompt. The proposed identity has not yet passed a recognition or preference study.

questions: Which examples belong together, without seeing their labels?
Which use would you choose for each, and why?
Which words are masked or mispronounced?
What should remain fixed across new songs?
What variation would break the identity?
review.method: Listen at comparable comfortable levels, shuffle the order, include headphones and speakers, and record disagreements. Do not infer recognition from a waveform or a successful render.
